title: Measure first, then improve the pipeline
text: Research design Measure first, then improve the pipeline The experiments were intentionally staged: establish a dense baseline, inspect its failures, reduce policy-space noise, test reranking, and only then evaluate answer generation. 01 HR corpus 5 fictional Markdown policies → 02 Chunking 400/80, 700/120, 1000/150 → 03 Nomic + Chroma Dense semantic retrieval → 04 Failure analysis Exact evidence + source relevance → 05 TF-IDF routing Select likely policy file(s) → 06 Optional reranker Cross-encoder Top-5 → Top-3 → 07 Qwen generation Grounded Top-3 context → 08 Evaluation RAGAS + secondary judge + manual check Stack Fully local baseline Embeddings: nomic-embed-text (768-D) Vector DB: ChromaDB Generator: qwen3:0.6b Local judge: qwen2.5:1.5b-instruct + RAGAS Evaluation principle Retrieval before generation Ground truth stores exact source evidence, allowing Hit@K, Recall@K, Precision@K and MRR to be measured without depending on the generator. Design constraint CPU-conscious Latency was measured because an improvement that is too expensive on CPU is not automatically the preferred system.
excerpt: The experiments were intentionally staged: establish a dense baseline, inspect its failures, reduce policy-space noise, test reranking, and only then evaluate answer generation. Embeddings: nomic-embed-text (768-D) Vector DB: ChromaDB Generator: qwen3:0.6b Local judge: qwen2.5:1.5b-instruct + RAGAS Ground truth stores exact source evidence, allowin

title: Dense baseline, then chunking and failure analysis
text: Evaluations 1–3 Dense baseline, then chunking and failure analysis The first 20-question benchmark showed that Top-3 coverage was already strong, but additional chunks often came from the wrong policy. Initial dense retrieval · 20 questions Metric K=1 K=3 K=5 Hit@K 0.800 1.000 1.000 Recall@K 0.775 1.000 1.000 Precision@K 0.800 0.367 0.220 MRR — — 0.883 Interpretation: the required evidence was normally present by Top-3, but extra retrieved chunks diluted precision. Chunking experiment Size / overlap Chunks Hit@1 Recall@1 Recall@3 Prec@3 MRR@5 400 / 80 38 0.800 0.725 0.950 0.383 0.892 700 / 120 22 0.800 0.775 1.000 0.367 0.883 1000 / 150 16 0.700 0.650 1.000 0.367 0.825 700 / 120 was selected: complete Recall@3 with fewer chunks than 400/80; 1000/150 reduced first-rank quality. Failure diagnosis: dense retrieval was usually finding the answer, but semantically similar language from unrelated HR policies could enter Top-3. This shifted the research question from “how do I retrieve more?” to “how do I keep the search space cleaner?”

title: Policy routing fixed the main source-level error
text: Evaluations 4–6 Policy routing fixed the main source-level error TF-IDF was used only to select likely policy files. Dense Nomic retrieval still ranked chunks inside that candidate search space. Query User question No manual keyword rules → Route TF-IDF policy scores Up to 2 candidate files; fallback when weak/ambiguous → Embed Nomic query vector search_query: prefix → Retrieve Chroma Top-3 Dense search within selected scope 20-question source-cleanliness result 15 / 60 wrong-policy chunks · dense → 2 / 60 wrong-policy chunks · routed ≈87% reduction in wrong-policy chunks. Questions containing any wrong-policy chunk dropped from 11/20 to 1/20 . Why a new metric was needed Exact Evidence Precision@3 stayed at 0.367 , because a correct-policy chunk can be useful without containing the exact evidence string. Source Precision@3 exposed the improvement: Dense only ~.750 TF-IDF + dense ~.967 Ranking on the original 20 questions 16 / 20 first evidence at rank 1 18 / 20 within rank 2 20 / 20 within rank 3 · MRR@3 0.883 Because all 20 questions already had correct evidence inside Top-3, the benchmark was too easy to meaningfully study reranking. This motivated a harder 100-question set.

title: Harder 100-question retrieval benchmark
text: Evaluations 7–9 Harder 100-question retrieval benchmark The benchmark deliberately includes paraphrases, scenarios, thresholds, negative conditions, location rules, approval conditions, historical/current distinctions and cross-policy questions. 64 hard questions 36 medium questions 51 multi-evidence 19 multi-source 100 total questions Final three-system comparison · Top-3 Metric Dense only TF-IDF + dense TF-IDF + dense + reranker Hit@1 0.730 0.790 0.840 Hit@3 0.990 1.000 1.000 Recall@3 0.938 0.938 0.947 Evidence Precision@3 0.420 0.413 0.420 Source Precision@3 0.847 0.950 0.963 MRR@3 0.850 0.888 0.917 Ranking-quality snapshot Dense · MRR@3 .850 Routed · MRR@3 .888 Reranked · MRR@3 .917 The cross-encoder improved first-relevant ranking for 11 questions, worsened 7, and left 82 unchanged. CPU latency trade-off Stage Average Nomic query embedding 64.32 ms Dense after embedding 1.76 ms TF-IDF + dense after embedding 2.97 ms TF-IDF + dense + reranker after embedding (cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2) 401.08 ms Approximate total retrieval: ~66 ms dense, ~67 ms routed dense, ~465 ms reranked. Selected retrieval design: TF-IDF + dense. The reranker achieved the best aggregate ranking metrics, but policy routing delivered most of the practical benefit for almost no additional CPU latency.
excerpt: The benchmark deliberately includes paraphrases, scenarios, thresholds, negative conditions, location rules, approval conditions, historical/current distinctions and cross-policy questions. The cross-encoder improved first-relevant ranking for 11 questions, worsened 7, and left 82 unchanged. Approximate total retrieval: ~66 ms dense, ~67 ms routed

title: Grounded generation and judge comparison
text: Evaluations 10–13 Grounded generation and judge comparison The generator was deliberately kept small so that retrieval and grounding quality remained visible rather than being masked by a large model's prior knowledge. Route TF-IDF Policy candidate selection → Retrieve Nomic + Chroma Top-3 context → Generate qwen3:0.6b Context-only HR answer → Judge A RAGAS + Qwen2.5 Local, reproducible → Judge B GPT-5.6 Sol Same saved answers; secondary evaluation Final four-case generation comparison · 100 questions Pipeline Judge Faithfulness Factual correctness Semantic similarity Answer relevancy Dense RAGAS + Qwen2.5 0.801 0.652 0.779 — TF-IDF + Dense RAGAS + Qwen2.5 0.754 0.668 0.778 — Dense GPT-5.6 Sol 0.831 0.753 — 0.912 TF-IDF + Dense GPT-5.6 Sol 0.848 0.775 — 0.921 Context changed 36 / 100 questions had different retrieved context after routing Answer changed 32 / 100 generated answers changed Manual judge check 5 representative questions reviewed manually GPT-5.6 Sol aligned much better with the manual judgments than the smaller local judge in this small spot-check. Interpretation: generation scores are diagnostic, not absolute truth. The disagreement between judges became a result in itself: evaluator quality can become an evaluation bottleneck.
excerpt: The generator was deliberately kept small so that retrieval and grounding quality remained visible rather than being masked by a large model's prior knowledge. GPT-5.6 Sol aligned much better with the manual judgments than the smaller local judge in this small spot-check.

title: A simple routing layer beat complexity on the accuracy/speed trade-off.
text: Main conclusion A simple routing layer beat complexity on the accuracy/speed trade-off. The project showed that retrieval should be diagnosed before adding heavier components. TF-IDF policy routing substantially cleaned the search space at negligible cost; cross-encoder reranking improved ranking further but added ~400 ms CPU latency. The resulting classical pipeline is preserved as the baseline for the GraphRAG study. Continue to GraphRAG → Inspect code and artifacts ↗
excerpt: The project showed that retrieval should be diagnosed before adding heavier components. TF-IDF policy routing substantially cleaned the search space at negligible cost; cross-encoder reranking improved ranking further but added ~400 ms CPU latency. The resulting classical pipeline is preserved as the baseline for the GraphRAG study.

title: Build the graph in validated stages
text: Research pipeline Build the graph in validated stages The graph is treated as an engineered representation, not as an automatic LLM by-product. Each intermediate stage is inspected before the next one is trusted. 08.1 Schema discovery spaCy candidates → embeddings → PCA/HDBSCAN → manual review → 08.2 Entity extraction GLiNER spans + type + confidence + offsets → 08.2.1 Entity validation Interactive full-corpus inspection → Next · 08.3 Relation extraction Build relations only after entity quality is validated → Future Neo4j + GraphRAG Validated graph retrieval compared with the classical RAG baseline
excerpt: The graph is treated as an engineered representation, not as an automatic LLM by-product. Each intermediate stage is inspected before the next one is trusted.

title: Let the corpus suggest the ontology, then review it manually
text: 08.1 · entity schema discovery Let the corpus suggest the ontology, then review it manually Candidate concepts were collected from the policy corpus, embedded with Nomic, projected with PCA, clustered with HDBSCAN, and manually reviewed into a domain-specific schema. Input HR policies Clean Markdown + 700/120 chunks → Candidates spaCy NER + noun phrases → Represent Nomic embeddings 768-dimensional vectors → Explore PCA + HDBSCAN Structure candidate concepts → Review Manual curation Merge, split, reject noisy clusters → Output 25 entity types Reviewed GLiNER schema PCA view of candidate concepts Clustering is used as a schema-discovery aid, not as final entity extraction. Cluster-size summary Manual review turns the discovered structure into a stable domain schema. Reviewed entity schema · 25 types MONEY_AMOUNT DURATION ORGANIZATION LEAVE_RULE APPROVAL_REQUIREMENT LEAVE_CONCEPT POLICY WORK_ARRANGEMENT REMOTE_WORK_ALLOWANCE BUSINESS_TRAVEL DATE TIME_PERIOD TIME_CONSTRAINT LIMIT HOTEL_RATE_LIMIT EXPENSE_CONCEPT JOB_ROLE ENTITLEMENT REQUIREMENT EMPLOYEE_TYPE COMPANY_RESOURCE EXCEPTION TRANSPORT_MODE COUNTRY CURRENCY
excerpt: Candidate concepts were collected from the policy corpus, embedded with Nomic, projected with PCA, clustered with HDBSCAN, and manually reviewed into a domain-specific schema.

title: Extract candidate spans with a deliberately low validation floor
text: 08.2 · GLiNER entity extraction Extract candidate spans with a deliberately low validation floor GLiNER receives the 25 reviewed labels and the original chunks. Each stored prediction preserves the exact span, canonical type, confidence, and character offsets. Schema 25 reviewed types Natural-language labels supplied to GLiNER + Text 20 chunks 5 policy documents → Model GLiNER medium v2.1 urchade/gliner_medium-v2.1 → Output 361 detections span + type + score + offsets Current extraction metadata Documents 5 Chunks 20 Chunk size / overlap 700 / 120 Schema size 25 types Stored detections 361 Unique entity/type pairs 198 Extraction floor 0.20 Confidence range 0.202 – 0.987 Mean confidence 0.586 Threshold experiment 212 detections at old ≥ 0.50 run 98 unique entity/type pairs → 361 detections at current ≥ 0.20 run 198 unique entity/type pairs The 0.20 threshold is an extraction floor for validation , not the final acceptance threshold. Lower-confidence candidates are intentionally retained so they can be inspected instead of discarded upstream. title: Relationship extraction comes next.
text: Next stage · 08.3 Relationship extraction comes next. The current GraphRAG work intentionally stops after entity validation. The next research stage will construct relationships between the validated entities before anything is loaded into Neo4j. Planned continuation Current Validated entities Finalize confidence threshold, spans and entity types → 08.3 Relation extraction Generate candidate relations between valid entity pairs → Validate Relation quality Inspect semantics, direction and consistency → Then Neo4j Load only validated graph structure → Evaluate GraphRAG Compare retrieval against the traditional RAG baseline Current boundary of this page: 08.1 schema discovery, 08.2 GLiNER entity extraction and 08.2.1 interactive entity validation are documented here. Relation extraction results will be added only after 08.3 is completed and validated.
